name: eve
description: The Open Framework for Building Agents
readmeExcerpt:
eve

[eve](https://eve.dev/) is a filesystem-first framework for durable AI agents. Core agent capabilities live in conventional locations, so projects are easier to inspect, extend, and operate. ## The filesystem is the authoring interface A typical eve agent has this structure: ```text my-agent/ └── agent/ ├── agent.ts # Optional: model and runtime config ├── instructions.md # Required: the always-on system prompt ├── tools/ # Optional: typed functions the model can call │ └── get_weather.ts ├── skills/ # Optional: procedures loaded on demand │ └── plan_a_trip.md ├── channels/ # Optional: message channels (HTTP, Slack, Discord) │ └── slack.ts └── schedules/ # Optional: recurring cron jobs └── weekly_recap.ts ``` Read the [documentation](https://eve.dev/docs) for the full project layout and guides. ## Quick start ```bash npx eve@latest init my-agent ``` This creates a new `my-agent` directory, installs its dependencies, initializes Git, and starts the interactive terminal UI. The generated agent uses `openai/gpt-6-luna-fast` with high reasoning. To start with another AI Gateway model, pass its model ID: ```bash npx eve@latest init my-agent --model openai/gpt-5.6-terra ``` Passing `--model` without `--reasoning` uses the provider's default reasoning. Pass `--reasoning` to set it explicitly. To add eve to an existing project, pass a path: ```bash cd myapp npx eve@latest init . ``` > [!NOTE] > The `eve` package includes its full documentation, so coding agents can read it locally from > `node_modules/eve/docs`. ### A minimal example The generated project includes an `agent` directory. Replace `agent/instructions.md` with: ```md You are a concise weather demo assistant. Tell users that the weather data is mocked. ``` Add a mock weather tool at `agent/tools/get_weather.ts`: ```ts import { defineTool } from "eve/tools"; import { z } from "zod"; export default defineTool({ description: "Return mock weather data for a city.", inputSchema: z.object({ city: z.string().min(1) }), async execute({ city }) { return { city, condition: "Sunny", temperatureF: 72 }; }, }); ``` Choose the model in `agent/agent.ts`: ```ts import { defineAgent } from "eve"; export default defineAgent({ model: "openai/gpt-6-luna-fast", reasoning: "high", }); ``` For a new scaffold, start the agent again: ```bash npm run dev ``` That's a working agent. Add human-in-the-loop prompts, subagents, and schedules as needed. ### Add Web Chat From your agent's directory, link a Vercel project and add Web Chat: ```bash npx eve link npx eve add channel/web ``` Choose a hosting layout, then **Sign in with Vercel** to provision authentication for members of the project's team. You can also select **Web Chat** from the terminal UI's `/add` channel picker. Run `npx eve deploy` when ready to publish. Local development works without browser sign-in. See the [Web Chat setup guide](https://eve.dev/docs/channels/eve#web-chat-with-sign-in-with-vercel) for permissions and recovery. ## Community The eve community lives on [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/vercel/eve/discussions), where you can ask questions, share ideas, and show what you've built. ## Contributing Contributions are welcome. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) to get the repo running locally and land a change, and use [issues](https://github.com/vercel/eve/issues) and [discussions](https://github.com/vercel/eve/discussions) to collaborate. By participating, you agree to our [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). ## Security Please do not open public issues for security vulnerabilities. Instead, follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) and report responsibly to [responsible.disclosure@vercel.com](mailto:responsible.disclosure@vercel.com).
readmeHtml:
eve

eve is a filesystem-first framework for durable AI agents. Core agent capabilities live in conventional locations, so projects are easier to inspect, extend, and operate.

The filesystem is the authoring interface

A typical eve agent has this structure:

my-agent/
└── agent/
    ├── agent.ts            # Optional: model and runtime config
    ├── instructions.md     # Required: the always-on system prompt
    ├── tools/              # Optional: typed functions the model can call
    │   └── get_weather.ts
    ├── skills/             # Optional: procedures loaded on demand
    │   └── plan_a_trip.md
    ├── channels/           # Optional: message channels (HTTP, Slack, Discord)
    │   └── slack.ts
    └── schedules/          # Optional: recurring cron jobs
        └── weekly_recap.ts

Read the documentation for the full project layout and guides.

Quick start

npx eve@latest init my-agent

This creates a new my-agent directory, installs its dependencies, initializes Git, and starts the interactive terminal UI. The generated agent uses openai/gpt-6-luna-fast with high reasoning.

To start with another AI Gateway model, pass its model ID:

npx eve@latest init my-agent --model openai/gpt-5.6-terra

Passing --model without --reasoning uses the provider's default reasoning. Pass --reasoning to set it explicitly.

To add eve to an existing project, pass a path:

cd myapp
npx eve@latest init .

Note

The eve package includes its full documentation, so coding agents can read it locally from node_modules/eve/docs.

A minimal example

The generated project includes an agent directory. Replace agent/instructions.md with:

You are a concise weather demo assistant. Tell users that the weather data is mocked.

Add a mock weather tool at agent/tools/get_weather.ts:

import { defineTool } from "eve/tools";
import { z } from "zod";

export default defineTool({
  description: "Return mock weather data for a city.",
  inputSchema: z.object({ city: z.string().min(1) }),
  async execute({ city }) {
    return { city, condition: "Sunny", temperatureF: 72 };
  },
});

Choose the model in agent/agent.ts:

import { defineAgent } from "eve";

export default defineAgent({
  model: "openai/gpt-6-luna-fast",
  reasoning: "high",
});

For a new scaffold, start the agent again:

npm run dev

That's a working agent. Add human-in-the-loop prompts, subagents, and schedules as needed.

Add Web Chat

From your agent's directory, link a Vercel project and add Web Chat:

npx eve link
npx eve add channel/web

Choose a hosting layout, then Sign in with Vercel to provision authentication for members of the project's team. You can also select Web Chat from the terminal UI's /add channel picker. Run npx eve deploy when ready to publish. Local development works without browser sign-in. See the Web Chat setup guide for permissions and recovery.

Community

The eve community lives on GitHub Discussions, where you can ask questions, share ideas, and show what you've built.

Contributing

Contributions are welcome. See CONTRIBUTING.md to get the repo running locally and land a change, and use issues and discussions to collaborate. By participating, you agree to our Code of Conduct.

Security

Please do not open public issues for security vulnerabilities. Instead, follow SECURITY.md and report responsibly to responsible.disclosure@vercel.com.

releases.name: eve@1.0.0-rc.13
releases.body:
Released 2026-11-12 · [Compare with 1.0.0-rc.12](https://github.com/vercel/eve/compare/eve%401.0.0-rc.12...eve%401.0.0-rc.13)

### Features

- eve now targets Node.js 26: new projects pin `engines.node` and `@types/node` to `26.x`, so Vercel deploys them on the `nodejs26.x` runtime, and the default sandbox image and generated Discord relay Dockerfile run Node.js 26.
  eve still supports Node.js 24 and later. When eve updates the `package.json` of an existing project that pins `engines.node` to another major, such as `24.x`, it now sets `26.x` and prints a warning. SvelteKit apps deployed to Vercel need `@sveltejs/adapter-vercel` 6.3.5 or later to build on Node.js 26. ([#6304](https://github.com/vercel/eve/pull/6304))

### Bug Fixes

- `eve dev` no longer answers every second request with an empty `400 Bad Request` when the client sends `Connection: close` and the agent replies with a keep-alive response such as an MCP SSE stream, as happens behind the `vercel dev` proxy. ([#6298](https://github.com/vercel/eve/pull/6298))

releases.name: eve@1.0.0-rc.12
releases.body:
Released 2026-11-12 · [Compare with 1.0.0-rc.11](https://github.com/vercel/eve/compare/eve%401.0.0-rc.11...eve%401.0.0-rc.12)

### Features

- Slack tool approvals now render as one card that holds the prompt, the tool input, and the **Approve** and **Deny** buttons.
  The card replaces the separate approval card and collapsed **Tool input** block. It lists up to 10 top-level input fields within a fixed size budget, and a batch of large approvals splits across messages, so a click's callback stays bounded however large the input is. Approvals without input keep the compact card. An answered approval keeps its input preview as a record of what was approved, where eve used to delete the separate tool-input message when the request ended.
  If you call `renderInteractionBlocks` from `eve/channels/slack`, an approval with tool input now returns one `container` block whose `child_blocks` hold the input preview and an `actions` block, instead of a `card` with `actions` followed by a **Tool input** container. Code that reads `actions` or stamps `block_id`s on interactive blocks should also look inside `child_blocks`. ([#6271](https://github.com/vercel/eve/pull/6271))

releases.name: eve@1.0.0-rc.11
releases.body:
Released 2026-11-12 · [Compare with 1.0.0-rc.10](https://github.com/vercel/eve/compare/eve%401.0.0-rc.10...eve%401.0.0-rc.11)

### Features

- Add `ctx.conversation.space`, which names the place a conversation happens, such as a Slack channel, so tools, approval policies, dynamic values, and memory scopes can share data per place.
  Slack, Discord, Teams, Telegram, Linq, Photon, and Chat SDK channels report a space with a stable `id` namespaced by platform and workspace, a `type` of `direct` or `shared`, a `visibility` of `public` or `private` when the platform says, and a `workspaceId` where the platform has one. Custom channels report theirs with a new `space({ state })` hook beside `audience`. Tools and memory scope resolvers can now read `ctx.conversation`, which dynamic values already had. ([#6111](https://github.com/vercel/eve/pull/6111))
- Add the experimental `eve/experimental/extensions/custom-skills` extension, which lets the people talking to an agent save their own versioned skills, for themselves or shared with everyone in a channel or group chat.

releases.name: eve@1.0.0-rc.10
releases.body:
Released 2026-11-11 · [Compare with 1.0.0-rc.9](https://github.com/vercel/eve/compare/eve%401.0.0-rc.9...eve%401.0.0-rc.10)

### Features

- `defineDynamic()` in `agent/tools/` can return a `defineWorkflowTool()` held by a top-level `const`, so a workflow tool can be offered only on some model calls.
  Its entry point can be written inline or reference a top-level `"use workflow"` function. The build fails when a workflow tool's entry point lacks `"use workflow"` or the tool is created inside the dynamic function. ([#6235](https://github.com/vercel/eve/pull/6235))
- Agents deployed to Vercel, including agents added to an app with `withEve`, now run schedules with Vercel Schedules through a private function instead of Vercel Cron Jobs.
  Each Vercel schedule is named after its file, such as `eve.billing.sweep` for `schedules/billing/sweep.ts`, and `withEve` agents add the agent's name, such as `eve.billing.heartbeat`. Building a `withEve` project requires Vercel CLI 65.14.0 or later. ([#6087](https://github.com/vercel/eve/pull/6087))
- Bundle the server faster in `eve build` and `eve dev` by resolving dependency imports and CommonJS path globals inside Rolldown instead of eve's Java

releases.name: @vercel/agent-runs@1.0.0-rc.6
releases.body:
Released 2026-11-12 · [Compare with 1.0.0-rc.5](https://github.com/vercel/eve/compare/%40vercel%2Fagent-runs%401.0.0-rc.5...%40vercel%2Fagent-runs%401.0.0-rc.6)

### Bug Fixes

- A context compaction's summary request during a turn now exports its own `chat <model>` span under the turn's `invoke_agent` span, with its token usage, cost, and `ai.settings.context.eve.compaction.request=summary`, so traces no longer undercount compacting turns.
  Model spans now also carry `agent.turn.id`. `@vercel/agent-runs` adds `TurnOperation.modelCall` for model calls a turn makes outside its steps.
  Thanks @zackleman for reporting this in #5922. ([#6251](https://github.com/vercel/eve/pull/6251))

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open, filesystem-first framework for building and orchestrating AI agents.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Eve is a robust framework created by Vercel designed to standardize the development and deployment of AI agents. It champions a strict filesystem-first methodology, meaning that agent definitions, capabilities, memory structures, and prompts are managed as standardized files within a repository rather than obscured in database configurations. This approach allows developers to leverage existing version control, CI/CD pipelines, and IDE features seamlessly when building complex, multi-agent systems. The framework provides the underlying infrastructure to connect these file-defined agents with various large language models and external APIs.
keyFeatures: Filesystem-First Design: Mandates that all agent logic, prompts, and configurations are stored as plain text files, enabling robust version control and easy auditing.
Standardized Agent Architecture: Provides a clear, opinionated structure for defining an agent's capabilities, inputs, and expected outputs.
Seamless Vercel Integration: Optimized for deployment on Vercel's infrastructure, allowing developers to spin up agentic workflows with minimal configuration.
Multi-Agent Orchestration: Includes primitives for coordinating complex tasks across multiple specialized agents working in tandem.
Open Framework: Built as an open-source standard to encourage interoperability and community-driven ecosystem growth.

useCases.title: Version-Controlled AI
useCases.description: Engineering teams build AI workflows where every prompt tweak and capability update is reviewed, diffed, and deployed via standard pull requests.

useCases.title: Serverless Agent Deployment
useCases.description: Developers rapidly deploy lightweight, specialized agents to edge functions using Vercel's hosting ecosystem for low-latency responses.

useCases.title: Complex Task Orchestration
useCases.description: Architects design systems where a planner agent delegates sub-tasks to highly specialized researcher and coder agents, all defined within the same repo.

useCases.title: CI/CD AI Testing
useCases.description: QA teams write automated tests against agent definitions stored in the filesystem to ensure behavioral consistency before production deployment.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Eve is for full-stack developers, AI engineers, and DevOps practitioners who want to bring software engineering best practices, such as version control and CI/CD, to the creation of AI agents. Familiarity with agent workflows is highly recommended for optimal usage.
